newsitem.title: USA: IRS probes Atlantic Beach, Fla. utility deal-paper.
newsitem.headline: IRS probes Atlantic Beach, Fla. utility deal-paper.

text.p: The U.S. Internal Revenue Service is examining a 1996 utilities revenue bond issue by Atlantic Beach, Fla., for possible tax law violations, the Jacksonville Times-Union said Wednesday.

In a May 30 letter to the north Florida municipality, Charles Anderson, manager of the IRS' southeast tax-exempt bond group, said the audit of the $22 million issue is part of a broader investigation into tax-exempt bonds.

IRS asked for documents relating to Atlantic Beach's selection of First Union Capital Markets Corp, a unit of First Union Corp, as financial adviser and William R. Hough & Co as lead underwriter on the issue, the newspaper said.

The agency also requested information about the selection of AMBAC Investment Corp Investment Corp, which handled the temporary investment of the bond proceeds for the city, the newspaper said. AMBAC is a unit of AMBAC Inc.

The city is complying with the IRS' request for documents, and has done nothing wrong, its bond counsel said. The three firms were selected in competitive bidding processes that are fully documented, attorney Sandy MacLennan said.
"I'm extremely confident that once we send the IRS what they want they'll say, 'Fine,'" MacLennan told the newspaper.
Neither MacLennan nor IRS officials could immediately be reached for comment Wednesday.
Atlantic Beach, which was under court order to fix sewer and drainage problems, issued the tax-exempt bonds to pay for improvements.

It was unclear what specifically the IRS was looking for. The newspaper said the probe may have been triggered by an Atlantic Beach resident who was a frequent critic of the bond issue and who had complained at city commission meetings that the deal involved unusually high investment fees and commissions. The city has disputed that allegation.
